result.topic_en: Euler finishes the numerical evaluation of the shape of a vibrating elastic rod at points u = 2/5, 3/5 and 4/5 of its length for ω = 5π/4, refers to Fig. 7 for the resulting curve with one node at O, and infers that the higher solutions (ω = 9π/4, etc.) will have two, three, … nodes.

$\omega = \frac{5\pi}{4}$ erit $\frac{2}{5}\omega = \frac{1}{2}\pi = 90^\circ$ et
$e^{\frac{2}{5}\omega} = 4,8104$ et $e^{-\frac{2}{5}\omega} = 0,2079$,
hincque colligitur:
$y = 5,8104 + 2576.0,7921 = 0,2079.$
IV. Sit nunc $u = \frac{3}{5}$, siue $s = \frac{3}{5}a$, eritque
$y = (e^{\frac{3}{5}\omega} + \sin.\frac{3}{5}\omega + \cos.\frac{3}{5}\omega) - e^{2\omega}(e^{-\frac{3}{5}\omega} - \sin.\frac{3}{5}\omega + \cos.\frac{3}{5}\omega)$,
vbi est
$\frac{3}{5}\omega = \frac{3}{4}\pi = 135^\circ$, ideoque
$e^{\frac{3}{5}\omega} = 10,550$ et $e^{-\frac{3}{5}\omega} = 0,0948$, hincque erit
$y = 10,550 + 2576.1,3194 = 3387.$
V. Sit nunc $u = \frac{4}{5}$, seu $s = \frac{4}{5}\omega$, ac fiet
$y = (e^{\frac{4}{5}\omega} + \sin.\frac{4}{5}\omega + \cos.\frac{4}{5}\omega) - e^{2\omega}(e^{-\frac{4}{5}\omega} - \sin.\frac{4}{5}\omega + \cos.\frac{4}{5}\omega)$
et ob
$\frac{4}{5}\omega = \pi = 180^\circ$; $e^{\frac{4}{5}\omega} = 23,140$ et $e^{-\frac{4}{5}\omega} = 0,0432$
erit
$y = 22,140 + 2576.0,9568 = 2487.$
Talis igitur forma quam virga inter vibrandum recipiet in Tabula (fig. 7.) exhibetur, vbi neminem offendat magnitudo applicatarum, quippe quae per numerum quempiam praegrandem diuisae sunt intelligendae. Haec ergo curua non nisi vnicum habet nodum in puncto O, vnde satis tuto concludere licet, sequentem curuam, quae ex valore $\omega = \frac{9\pi}{4}$ nascitur, habituram esse duos nodos, sequentem tres, et ita porro.
[margin:] Tab. II. Fig. 7.

items.quote: Haec ergo curua non nisi vnicum habet nodum in puncto O, vnde satis tuto concludere licet, sequentem curuam, quae ex valore $\omega = \frac{9\pi}{4}$ nascitur, habituram esse duos nodos, sequentem tres, et ita porro.
items.english: This curve therefore has only a single node, at the point O, from which one may fairly safely conclude that the next curve, arising from the value ω = 9π/4, will have two nodes, the following one three, and so on.
